name: Coal Phase-Out
description: Rapid deployment of solar infrastructure to phase out coal and thermal generation, reducing emissions while maintaining grid stability across El Salvador.

economics.investment_breakdown: Utility-scale solar farms ($180M), rooftop solar programs ($80M), battery storage systems ($70M), grid integration ($50M)
economics.economic_loss_explanation: Avoided fossil fuel costs, reduced emissions penalties, health benefits from cleaner air, grid stability improvements
economics.roi_explanation: Every $1 invested generates $2.20 in combined energy savings, health benefits, and economic growth over 10 years

ai_analysis.executive_summary: Ambitious renewable energy transition demonstrates feasibility of coal phase-out with 50% solar capacity increase. Significant reductions in grid stress across all regions, with only San Salvador requiring moderate attention. This scenario positions El Salvador as a regional climate leader while achieving energy independence and economic benefits.

priority_actions.action: Deploy 250MW utility-scale solar farms in Usulután and La Paz
priority_actions.impact: Provides baseload renewable capacity, reduces fossil fuel dependency by 40%

priority_actions.action: Implement residential rooftop solar program nationwide
priority_actions.impact: Distributes generation across grid, reduces peak demand by 15%
Smooths solar intermittency, enables 24/7 renewable power

regional_breakdown.analysis: Capital benefits significantly from distributed solar deployment but still experiences moderate stress during peak evening hours. 48 MWh deficit down from baseline 95 MWh - represents 50% improvement.
regional_breakdown.recommendation: Prioritize battery storage deployment near major substations. Accelerate commercial building solar mandates. Implement smart grid systems for demand response.

regional_breakdown.analysis: Western region sees substantial benefits from new solar capacity. Industrial zone solar installations provide daytime generation aligned with demand patterns.
regional_breakdown.recommendation: Continue solar farm expansion in agricultural areas. Partner with coffee cooperatives for agrivoltaic projects combining farming and solar generation.

regional_breakdown.analysis: Remaining 12 regions operate well within safe parameters. Distributed solar deployment has successfully reduced transmission losses and improved local resilience.
regional_breakdown.recommendation: Focus on maintenance and optimization. Deploy community solar programs for rural electrification. Monitor for opportunities to export surplus generation.

risks: Solar intermittency requires robust storage and backup systems
Initial capital investment high - financing critical
Skilled workforce needed for installation and maintenance
Grid modernization essential to handle distributed generation
opportunities: Position El Salvador as renewable energy leader in Central America
Export surplus solar capacity to neighboring countries
Attract green industry and data centers with cheap renewable power
Create 5,000+ jobs in renewable energy sector
Reduce air pollution - health benefits worth $120M annually
